---
applyTo: "src/ui/webview-react/store/**"
---

<purpose>
Stores are split by ownership, not by screen. Extend the store that owns the data source instead of creating mirrored state in multiple stores.
</purpose>

<ownership>
- `workflowStore` owns execution state, live output, history snapshots, retry state, context-window stats, and undo metadata. Streaming updates should land here, not in component-local state.
- `uiStore` owns persisted view preferences and transient modal/navigation state. It uses `persist` + `vsCodeRawStorage`, so stored shapes must stay JSON-serializable.
- `editorStore` owns draft editing state. New-step drafts are persisted through `vscode.getState()`, while edits to existing steps live in workflow-local `pendingEdits` keyed by `queue:index` or `finalStep`.
- `settingsStore` keeps both raw global settings and workflow overrides. Effective-value helpers are the canonical inheritance path.
- `terminalStore` tracks session metadata only; xterm instances, DOM, and replay buffers stay outside Zustand in `terminalRegistry.ts`.
- `workspaceViewerStore` persists modal state and file drafts. Its file keys are normalized workspace-relative forward-slash paths so navigation from output/search/diff reuses the same cache entries.
</ownership>

<gotchas>
- `workflowStore.syncIncomingWorkflowProperties()` keeps workflow-property undo snapshots in sync. Skipping it makes workflow undo/redo incomplete.
- `historyOutputs` is a separate historical snapshot; continuation runs may promote old history back into `liveOrderedEntries`, so do not collapse those concepts into one array.
- `runtimeUndoGeneration` exists for undoable actions that only change runtime metadata. Bump it instead of mutating unrelated state just to force a zundo snapshot.
- **Whether a step edit is undoable is decided by `isStepContentEqual` (exported here) — it is the single source of truth and must stay the only place that lists step fields.** It backs both the zundo `equality` option below and `useMessageHandler.ts`'s `STEPS_EXTENDED` content-diff (`shouldRecord`). It used to be two independently hand-written field allow-lists (`prompt`/`name`/`model`/`harness`/`enabled`, slightly different between the two copies); any step property missing from *both* — e.g. `resumeSession`, `mcpServers`, `toolPermissions`, `additionalArgs` — silently never registered as undoable no matter which property drawer wrote it, because `STEPS_EXTENDED` paused around the write before zundo's own equality even ran. Now it's a real deep-equal over every field except the runtime-only ones (`status`, `_runtime`), so a newly added `PromptStep`/`ScriptStep` field is covered automatically — don't reintroduce a per-field list at either call site. This was only half of "step edits aren't undoable" — even with `isStepContentEqual` recording the entry correctly, the server-side echo pattern documented in `ui.instructions.md` (`publishViewIdentity` vs. `refreshDefinitionMutationView`) could still wipe that same entry moments later; both had to be fixed together.
- Prefer defined store actions over raw `setState`, except for the few centralized bootstrap/reset flows that intentionally touch multiple slices at once.
- `uiStore` holds two different views of "the executing run's state", and only one of them is live. `runSummaries` (with `executionRunRef`) is a **snapshot frozen at the last `RUN_VIEW_LOADED`** — nothing refreshes it as a run moves running → pausing → paused, so a run seeded and started in one gesture leaves its summary reading `idle` for the run's entire life (`markExecutionRunFinished` only patches it on terminal states). `loadedWorkflows` is the **live** mirror of every active workflow, kept current by `WORKFLOW_ADDED` / `WORKFLOW_SUMMARY_UPDATED` / `WORKFLOW_DISMISSED`. Read live execution state from `loadedWorkflows` and treat the snapshot as a fallback only; reading it the other way round is what once made the header show "Nothing is executing" (disabled Pause/Stop, no Resume) while a run was genuinely paused, and suppressed the pausing banner outright. `getWorkflowExecutionControls` now additionally ignores any non-active `executionRunState` as a backstop.
- **`phase` is part of the CLI entry identity tuple `(target, runIndex, attemptIndex, phase)`, and *every* live matcher must use the whole tuple** — go through `matchesCliEntryIdentity`, never hand-roll a subset. One step's pre-condition, prompt, and end-condition all share the first three fields, so a phase-blind match silently attaches one phase's output to another's row. That was the bug behind "the prompt's output never reached the output pane": `appendStreamingEvents` matched without `phase`, so on a step whose pre-condition ran first, every structured event the harness streamed was merged into the pre-condition's script row and the prompt's own row stayed empty for the whole run. Treat an omitted `phase` as `EXECUTION_PHASES.PROMPT` when matching (`overlayLiveHistoryEntries`/`findMatchingCliEntryIndex` do), but persisted prompt entries intentionally omit that default phase — do not normalize them to a serialized `:phase:prompt` key, or live output duplicates instead of overlaying.
- **Output rows are ordered by `timestampMs` (`sortOutputMessages`), not by arrival or array position**, on both the live and history paths. Anything that stamps a CLI entry is therefore deciding where it renders, and a back-dated entry silently jumps to the top of the pane rather than appearing where it was produced — see the `promptStartedAt` bullet in `core.instructions.md` for the executor-side invariant this depends on.
- `loadedWorkflows` mirrors the orchestrator's *instance registry*, so membership means "loaded here", not "executing here". `getWorkflowSummaries()` returns every entry in `WorkflowOrchestrator.instances`, and every created/loaded instance is put there (`createWorkflow`, `loadFreshInstanceAndReplay`) — not only executing ones, despite the comment near `executeWorkflow` saying otherwise; the active-state narrowing happens client-side in the `WORKFLOWS_LIST` handler. RUNNING/PAUSING therefore imply a live run, but **PAUSED does not**: merely opening a lineage whose latest run was left paused on disk hydrates an instance in that state, which is why the same lineage would appear and disappear from the dropdown's pinned Running region depending on whether this host session happened to hold its instance. Anything that must mean "executed in this session" needs `uiStore.observedRunningWorkflowIds` (admitted on RUNNING/PAUSING, retained across a following PAUSED, pruned with the instance, never persisted), not a state predicate. Note a paused run also holds no runner lock — `WorkflowExecutor.confirmPauseAndStop` returns out of the executor and `WorkflowInstance.startWorkflowExecution`'s `finally` releases it — so lock presence is not a fallback signal either.
- Snapshot-apply actions (`loadWorkflow`, `loadHistoryRun`, `hydrateLiveRunHistory`) run incoming data through `preserveReferences` (`utils/structuralSharing.ts`) so a replayed-but-unchanged snapshot keeps existing object identities — this is what keeps the output pane's memo chain (`useOutputRowsModel` → `buildOutputRows` → row memos) from redrawing unchanged rows. Two rules keep it working: don't pre-clear state an action will immediately replace (the `RUN_VIEW_LOADED` handler passes `skipHistoryOutputsClear` for exactly this), and only pass `loadWorkflow`'s `preserveLiveOutput` for a same-address, same-definition-revision, non-rollback replay — anything else must clear runtime state.
- `uiStore.displayedViewAddress` is the *navigation target*, not proof that `workflowStore` holds its content. `WORKFLOW_VIEW_IDENTITY` (and the optimistic step in `requestRunViewLoad`) can advance `displayedViewAddress`/`displayedDefinitionRevision` to a new lineage before that lineage's own `RUN_VIEW_LOADED` ever applies — e.g. a reconnect replay whose snapshot the stale-guard rejected. `appliedViewAddress` is the separate, non-persisted field that only `markViewAddressApplied` sets, and only right after `useWorkflowStore.loadWorkflow(...)` actually runs in the `RUN_VIEW_LOADED` handler. Two places must key off `appliedViewAddress`, not `displayedViewAddress`: the `RUN_VIEW_LOADED` regressive-snapshot guard (comparing against `displayedViewAddress` there means a snapshot for the *new* address gets judged against the *previous* workflow's still-resident content and is rejected forever) and `navigateToWorkflowAddress`'s no-op short-circuit (otherwise a click on the workflow that should recover from exactly that state no-ops because the address already "matches"). A requestless `ACTIVE_WORKFLOW_CHANGED` starts an authoritative full replay and must clear `appliedViewAddress` even when the instance ID is unchanged: a resumed mobile page can retain workflow content that no longer matches its retained address, and treating the following snapshot as a same-address regression leaves the header on that unrelated name. This was the root cause of workflow switches/reconnects showing the previous workflow's title/steps indefinitely.
</gotchas>
